Pathway 2 directly connects Estramustine to Prostate Cancer, which is also associated with Radium Ra 223 Dichloride, a known inhibitor of prostate cancer progression. Both pathways indicate that Estramustine may exert a role in the development or progression of prostate cancer, though the exact mechanism is not fully elucidated. The high scores in both paths suggest a strong potential for Estramustine to be repurposed for the treatment of prostate carcinoma, though further research is needed to confirm this relationship and understand the underlying biological mechanisms.
